# kubesense_dashboard (Resource)

A KubeSense dashboard, its panels, variables and layout written as blocks. Export to Terraform in the KubeSense UI writes this for an existing dashboard. Members the schema cannot type are set with jsonencode() in *_json attributes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Panels, variables and layout as blocks. Export to Terraform in the KubeSense
# UI writes this for an existing dashboard; members Terraform cannot type are
# *_json attributes set with jsonencode().
resource "kubesense_dashboard" "checkout" {
  name        = "Checkout"
  description = "Golden signals for checkout"

  grid_layout {
    h = 8
    i = "p1"
    w = 12
    x = 0
    y = 0
  }

  panel {
    name       = "CPU by pod"
    panel_type = "timeSeries"

    query {
      label         = "A"
      promql        = "sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total[5m])) by (pod)"
      query_mode    = "code"
      selected_mode = "metrics"
    }
  }

  variable {
    description = "Cluster to show"
    name        = "cluster"

    meta {
      default_value = "prod"
      value_json    = jsonencode("prod")
      variable_type = "textbox"
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Dashboard name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Dashboard description.
- `event_overlay` (Block List) Event markers drawn on every timeseries and bar panel that inherits them.
Absent means none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--event_overlay))
- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `grid_layout` (Block List) Positions for the top-level panels. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--grid_layout))
- `panel` (Block List) Top-level panels, outside any sub-grid. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel))
- `sub_grid` (Block List) Collapsible groups, each with its own panels and layout. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid))
- `sub_grid_layout` (Block List) Positions for the sub-grids within the dashboard. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid_layout))
- `tab` (Block List) Tabs, each with a page of its own. Empty or absent means the dashboard is
untabbed and its page is the top level above. When non-empty, the
top-level panels, gridLayout, subGrids and subGridLayout must all be
empty; they stay present so an older reader still parses the document.
Variables, event overlays and publicDashboardPath stay at the top level
and apply to every tab. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab))
- `variable` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--variable))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the dashboard was created (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Dashboard id.
- `updated_at` (String) When the dashboard was last changed (RFC 3339).

### Nested Schema for `panel.config.value_options`

Optional:

- `calculation` (String) Optional on purpose. Absent means the number is computed over the whole

<a id="nestedblock--panel--query"></a>
### Nested Schema for `panel.query`

Optional:

- `aggregation_json` (String) Set with jsonencode().
- `chart_type` (String)
- `color_preference` (String)
- `column_field` (Block List) No .catch() on this one in the zod — the only member of the base without a
fallback. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--column_field))
- `display` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--display))
- `display_format` (String)
- `expression` (String)
- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `field_config` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--field_config))
- `filter` (Block, Optional) Which monitors a panel draws when it does not name them, or how it narrows
the ones it names. Every key present must match; within types and within
states any one value matches.

Labels are a map here and a list of "key:value" on the wire: the renderer
sends them as `labels` to POST /api/synthetics/uptimes. Types go as `types`.
That endpoint does not filter by state, so a states filter is resolved
through GET /api/synthetics/monitors?state=…, which carries each monitor's
state, and the uptimes are then fetched for the ids it returns. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--filter))
- `filter_mode` (String)
- `filters_json` (String) Label matchers for builder mode, keyed by label. Each value's prefix picks
its PromQL operator: `v` is `label="v"`, `-v` is `label!="v"`, `~re` is
`label=~"re"` and `-~re` is `label!~"re"`. So `-` alone excludes the empty
value (`label!=""`). A whole `$var` or `-$var` value stands for the
variable's selected values. Set with jsonencode().
- `function` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--function))
- `group_by` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--group_by))
- `group_by_dimensions` (List of String) Sections around the outermost level's tiles. Only dimensions that level
carries are accepted by kubeapi; a host has no namespace. Not `groupBy`,
which the logs and traces arms use for a list of field objects.
- `label` (String)
- `label_options_json` (String) labelOptionsSchema :344 — discriminated on `type`, defaulting to auto
(DEFAULT_LABEL_OPTIONS :133).

Three arms for two cases. The first is the concrete default instance, and it
has to be written with plain fields rather than `!` — a required field is
never concrete, so `*#AutoLabelOptions` would leave nothing for the default to
materialise. But a closed concrete arm rejects any member added later, and
unlike `aggregation` or `sortBy` the auto case had no open sibling to fall
through to: `{type: "auto", somethingNew: 1}` matched neither arm. #AutoLabel
is that sibling. Set with jsonencode().
- `level` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--level))
- `list` (List of String)
- `monitor_ids` (List of String) The monitors to draw, in display order unless display.sort says
otherwise. An id that no longer exists is reported by the API and
skipped.
- `objective_id` (String) The objective "single" draws. "" means none picked yet, which the webapp
renders as an empty panel rather than fetching.
- `objective_name` (String) The objective's name AS IT WAS when the panel was saved. A cache, not an
identifier — objectiveId is what names the SLO.

Persisted so an editor can label its picker before the lookup returns, and
so a DELETED objective can still be named rather than shown as a bare
uuid. Readers must prefer the live name: a rename would otherwise leave
every dashboard asserting the old one forever.
- `pagination` (Block, Optional) explorerPaginationSchema :369, defaulting to DEFAULT_PAGINATION :146. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--pagination))
- `promql` (String)
- `query` (String)
- `query_mode` (String)
- `rule_id` (String) The rule "graph" and "value" draw. "" means none picked yet, which the
webapp renders as an empty panel rather than fetching.
- `rule_name` (String) The rule's name AS IT WAS when the panel was saved. A cache, not an
identifier — ruleId is what names the rule.

Persisted so an editor can label its picker before the lookup returns, and
so a DELETED rule can still be named rather than shown as a bare uuid.
Readers must prefer the live name: a rename would otherwise leave every
dashboard asserting the old one forever.
- `selected_metric` (String) DEFAULT_METRIC :35. The editor substitutes this placeholder when the field
is missing and then PERSISTS it on the next save, so an omitted
selectedMetric is not neutral — it silently becomes a real query against an
unrelated metric.
- `selected_mode` (String)
- `selector_modifiers` (Block, Optional) Offset and @ on the series selector. The builder renders them once, where
the selector is first consumed: after its window, as in
`rate(m[5m] offset 1h @ end())`, or after the bare selector when nothing
windows it. Never between a selector and its window, which does not parse. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--selector_modifiers))
- `show_error_budget` (Boolean) Show each window's remaining error budget beside its compliance. Both
numbers are already on every SLO row, so this costs no extra request.
- `slo_table_view` (String)
- `sort_by` (String)
- `sort_order` (String)
- `sorting` (Block, Optional) sortingSchema :357, defaulting to DEFAULT_SORTING :137. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--panel--query--sorting))
- `source` (String)
- `summary_type` (String) Scopes "summary" like `filters`. Defaults to "monitor", which is what the
widget did before this field existed — an older saved panel keeps its
behaviour rather than silently changing what each row means.
- `time_windows_json` (String) Which rollup windows "single" draws.

These four and no others, because these are the four the API computes.
getSLOMetricsForSLOs builds one CTE per window with a literal INTERVAL, so
the set is fixed server-side rather than parameterised — a document naming
"90 days" would describe a column no response carries. Widen this only
together with the query and the columns.

"last_28_days" is four whole weeks, deliberately not 30 days. Set with jsonencode().
- `value` (String)
- `variables` (List of String)
- `view_mode` (String) What "single" draws: the objective's own rollups, a per-group breakdown,
or both. Only meaningful for a GROUPED objective — the webapp falls back
to the rollups when a panel names an SLO with no groups, so a saved
document does not blank itself if its SLO changes shape.
- `visible` (Boolean)
- `viz_type` (String)
- `widget_type` (String) "single", not "summary": an unconfigured panel waits for an objective
rather than fetching a fleet-wide rollup nobody asked for. The webapp
moved to that default in #2388 and this side was missed, so a panel saved
without the field meant one widget to the browser and another to
ApplyDefaults. The two must agree — this is the number the published
schema hands every other consumer.
- `window` (String) The window the uptime covers, ending now. Absent, the panel's time range
applies: its config.timeFrame, else the dashboard's.
- `xaxis` (String) SPL/SQL-only visualisation hints (:642-656). "auto" means the formatter
infers the column.
- `yaxis_json` (String) yaxis is a LIST, not a string. It was a string until commit 2c8d7ab1a
(2026-08-07, "update y-axis handling to support multiple select"), which
changed the persisted type and added coerceYaxisColumns + yaxisColumnsSchema
(:571, :586) plus a coercion step in migrateToNewSchema (:854) so stored
documents holding `yaxis: "cpu"` keep that selection.

Worth noting what that change cost: it is a breaking type change to a
persisted field, and it is detected by sniffing `!Array.isArray(next.yaxis)`
because panels carry no version marker. With one, the migration would key
off the version instead of guessing from shape. Set with jsonencode().

<a id="nestedblock--panel--query--column_field"></a>
### Nested Schema for `panel.query.column_field`

Optional:

- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `field` (String) The field name to query.
- `is_attribute` (Boolean) Whether this is an attribute field.
- `type` (String) The data type of the field. Defaults to "string" rather than being
required, because stored rules genuinely arrive without it — a live traces
rule with 119 firing series carries
`groupBy: [{field: "workload", is_attribute: false}]` and no type at all.
Requiring it rejected a document the product itself wrote and is running.

"string" is the safe fill: a group-by key is a string, and the two places a
NUMERIC type is load-bearing declare their own, so an aggregation cannot
silently acquire a string column.

- `sort` (String) How rows are ordered. Unset, they keep the order the API returned: the

automatic, with the display title derived from the query at render time

placeholder for one — and a panel that omits the key entirely means the

<a id="nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sub_grid.panel.query`

Optional:

- `aggregation_json` (String) Set with jsonencode().
- `chart_type` (String)
- `color_preference` (String)
- `column_field` (Block List) No .catch() on this one in the zod — the only member of the base without a
fallback. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--column_field))
- `display` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--display))
- `display_format` (String)
- `expression` (String)
- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `field_config` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--field_config))
- `filter` (Block, Optional) Which monitors a panel draws when it does not name them, or how it narrows
the ones it names. Every key present must match; within types and within
states any one value matches.

Labels are a map here and a list of "key:value" on the wire: the renderer
sends them as `labels` to POST /api/synthetics/uptimes. Types go as `types`.
That endpoint does not filter by state, so a states filter is resolved
through GET /api/synthetics/monitors?state=…, which carries each monitor's
state, and the uptimes are then fetched for the ids it returns. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--filter))
- `filter_mode` (String)
- `filters_json` (String) Label matchers for builder mode, keyed by label. Each value's prefix picks
its PromQL operator: `v` is `label="v"`, `-v` is `label!="v"`, `~re` is
`label=~"re"` and `-~re` is `label!~"re"`. So `-` alone excludes the empty
value (`label!=""`). A whole `$var` or `-$var` value stands for the
variable's selected values. Set with jsonencode().
- `function` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--function))
- `group_by` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--group_by))
- `group_by_dimensions` (List of String) Sections around the outermost level's tiles. Only dimensions that level
carries are accepted by kubeapi; a host has no namespace. Not `groupBy`,
which the logs and traces arms use for a list of field objects.
- `label` (String)
- `label_options_json` (String) labelOptionsSchema :344 — discriminated on `type`, defaulting to auto
(DEFAULT_LABEL_OPTIONS :133).

Three arms for two cases. The first is the concrete default instance, and it
has to be written with plain fields rather than `!` — a required field is
never concrete, so `*#AutoLabelOptions` would leave nothing for the default to
materialise. But a closed concrete arm rejects any member added later, and
unlike `aggregation` or `sortBy` the auto case had no open sibling to fall
through to: `{type: "auto", somethingNew: 1}` matched neither arm. #AutoLabel
is that sibling. Set with jsonencode().
- `level` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--level))
- `list` (List of String)
- `monitor_ids` (List of String) The monitors to draw, in display order unless display.sort says
otherwise. An id that no longer exists is reported by the API and
skipped.
- `objective_id` (String) The objective "single" draws. "" means none picked yet, which the webapp
renders as an empty panel rather than fetching.
- `objective_name` (String) The objective's name AS IT WAS when the panel was saved. A cache, not an
identifier — objectiveId is what names the SLO.

Persisted so an editor can label its picker before the lookup returns, and
so a DELETED objective can still be named rather than shown as a bare
uuid. Readers must prefer the live name: a rename would otherwise leave
every dashboard asserting the old one forever.
- `pagination` (Block, Optional) explorerPaginationSchema :369, defaulting to DEFAULT_PAGINATION :146. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--pagination))
- `promql` (String)
- `query` (String)
- `query_mode` (String)
- `rule_id` (String) The rule "graph" and "value" draw. "" means none picked yet, which the
webapp renders as an empty panel rather than fetching.
- `rule_name` (String) The rule's name AS IT WAS when the panel was saved. A cache, not an
identifier — ruleId is what names the rule.

Persisted so an editor can label its picker before the lookup returns, and
so a DELETED rule can still be named rather than shown as a bare uuid.
Readers must prefer the live name: a rename would otherwise leave every
dashboard asserting the old one forever.
- `selected_metric` (String) DEFAULT_METRIC :35. The editor substitutes this placeholder when the field
is missing and then PERSISTS it on the next save, so an omitted
selectedMetric is not neutral — it silently becomes a real query against an
unrelated metric.
- `selected_mode` (String)
- `selector_modifiers` (Block, Optional) Offset and @ on the series selector. The builder renders them once, where
the selector is first consumed: after its window, as in
`rate(m[5m] offset 1h @ end())`, or after the bare selector when nothing
windows it. Never between a selector and its window, which does not parse. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--selector_modifiers))
- `show_error_budget` (Boolean) Show each window's remaining error budget beside its compliance. Both
numbers are already on every SLO row, so this costs no extra request.
- `slo_table_view` (String)
- `sort_by` (String)
- `sort_order` (String)
- `sorting` (Block, Optional) sortingSchema :357, defaulting to DEFAULT_SORTING :137. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--sorting))
- `source` (String)
- `summary_type` (String) Scopes "summary" like `filters`. Defaults to "monitor", which is what the
widget did before this field existed — an older saved panel keeps its
behaviour rather than silently changing what each row means.
- `time_windows_json` (String) Which rollup windows "single" draws.

These four and no others, because these are the four the API computes.
getSLOMetricsForSLOs builds one CTE per window with a literal INTERVAL, so
the set is fixed server-side rather than parameterised — a document naming
"90 days" would describe a column no response carries. Widen this only
together with the query and the columns.

"last_28_days" is four whole weeks, deliberately not 30 days. Set with jsonencode().
- `value` (String)
- `variables` (List of String)
- `view_mode` (String) What "single" draws: the objective's own rollups, a per-group breakdown,
or both. Only meaningful for a GROUPED objective — the webapp falls back
to the rollups when a panel names an SLO with no groups, so a saved
document does not blank itself if its SLO changes shape.
- `visible` (Boolean)
- `viz_type` (String)
- `widget_type` (String) "single", not "summary": an unconfigured panel waits for an objective
rather than fetching a fleet-wide rollup nobody asked for. The webapp
moved to that default in #2388 and this side was missed, so a panel saved
without the field meant one widget to the browser and another to
ApplyDefaults. The two must agree — this is the number the published
schema hands every other consumer.
- `window` (String) The window the uptime covers, ending now. Absent, the panel's time range
applies: its config.timeFrame, else the dashboard's.
- `xaxis` (String) SPL/SQL-only visualisation hints (:642-656). "auto" means the formatter
infers the column.
- `yaxis_json` (String) yaxis is a LIST, not a string. It was a string until commit 2c8d7ab1a
(2026-08-07, "update y-axis handling to support multiple select"), which
changed the persisted type and added coerceYaxisColumns + yaxisColumnsSchema
(:571, :586) plus a coercion step in migrateToNewSchema (:854) so stored
documents holding `yaxis: "cpu"` keep that selection.

Worth noting what that change cost: it is a breaking type change to a
persisted field, and it is detected by sniffing `!Array.isArray(next.yaxis)`
because panels carry no version marker. With one, the migration would key
off the version instead of guessing from shape. Set with jsonencode().

<a id="nestedblock--sub_grid--panel--query--column_field"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sub_grid.panel.query.column_field`

Optional:

- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `field` (String) The field name to query.
- `is_attribute` (Boolean) Whether this is an attribute field.
- `type` (String) The data type of the field. Defaults to "string" rather than being
required, because stored rules genuinely arrive without it — a live traces
rule with 119 firing series carries
`groupBy: [{field: "workload", is_attribute: false}]` and no type at all.
Requiring it rejected a document the product itself wrote and is running.

"string" is the safe fill: a group-by key is a string, and the two places a
NUMERIC type is load-bearing declare their own, so an aggregation cannot
silently acquire a string column.

<a id="nestedblock--tab--panel--query"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tab.panel.query`

Optional:

- `aggregation_json` (String) Set with jsonencode().
- `chart_type` (String)
- `color_preference` (String)
- `column_field` (Block List) No .catch() on this one in the zod — the only member of the base without a
fallback. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--column_field))
- `display` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--display))
- `display_format` (String)
- `expression` (String)
- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `field_config` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--field_config))
- `filter` (Block, Optional) Which monitors a panel draws when it does not name them, or how it narrows
the ones it names. Every key present must match; within types and within
states any one value matches.

Labels are a map here and a list of "key:value" on the wire: the renderer
sends them as `labels` to POST /api/synthetics/uptimes. Types go as `types`.
That endpoint does not filter by state, so a states filter is resolved
through GET /api/synthetics/monitors?state=…, which carries each monitor's
state, and the uptimes are then fetched for the ids it returns. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--filter))
- `filter_mode` (String)
- `filters_json` (String) Label matchers for builder mode, keyed by label. Each value's prefix picks
its PromQL operator: `v` is `label="v"`, `-v` is `label!="v"`, `~re` is
`label=~"re"` and `-~re` is `label!~"re"`. So `-` alone excludes the empty
value (`label!=""`). A whole `$var` or `-$var` value stands for the
variable's selected values. Set with jsonencode().
- `function` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--function))
- `group_by` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--group_by))
- `group_by_dimensions` (List of String) Sections around the outermost level's tiles. Only dimensions that level
carries are accepted by kubeapi; a host has no namespace. Not `groupBy`,
which the logs and traces arms use for a list of field objects.
- `label` (String)
- `label_options_json` (String) labelOptionsSchema :344 — discriminated on `type`, defaulting to auto
(DEFAULT_LABEL_OPTIONS :133).

Three arms for two cases. The first is the concrete default instance, and it
has to be written with plain fields rather than `!` — a required field is
never concrete, so `*#AutoLabelOptions` would leave nothing for the default to
materialise. But a closed concrete arm rejects any member added later, and
unlike `aggregation` or `sortBy` the auto case had no open sibling to fall
through to: `{type: "auto", somethingNew: 1}` matched neither arm. #AutoLabel
is that sibling. Set with jsonencode().
- `level` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--level))
- `list` (List of String)
- `monitor_ids` (List of String) The monitors to draw, in display order unless display.sort says
otherwise. An id that no longer exists is reported by the API and
skipped.
- `objective_id` (String) The objective "single" draws. "" means none picked yet, which the webapp
renders as an empty panel rather than fetching.
- `objective_name` (String) The objective's name AS IT WAS when the panel was saved. A cache, not an
identifier — objectiveId is what names the SLO.

Persisted so an editor can label its picker before the lookup returns, and
so a DELETED objective can still be named rather than shown as a bare
uuid. Readers must prefer the live name: a rename would otherwise leave
every dashboard asserting the old one forever.
- `pagination` (Block, Optional) explorerPaginationSchema :369, defaulting to DEFAULT_PAGINATION :146. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--pagination))
- `promql` (String)
- `query` (String)
- `query_mode` (String)
- `rule_id` (String) The rule "graph" and "value" draw. "" means none picked yet, which the
webapp renders as an empty panel rather than fetching.
- `rule_name` (String) The rule's name AS IT WAS when the panel was saved. A cache, not an
identifier — ruleId is what names the rule.

Persisted so an editor can label its picker before the lookup returns, and
so a DELETED rule can still be named rather than shown as a bare uuid.
Readers must prefer the live name: a rename would otherwise leave every
dashboard asserting the old one forever.
- `selected_metric` (String) DEFAULT_METRIC :35. The editor substitutes this placeholder when the field
is missing and then PERSISTS it on the next save, so an omitted
selectedMetric is not neutral — it silently becomes a real query against an
unrelated metric.
- `selected_mode` (String)
- `selector_modifiers` (Block, Optional) Offset and @ on the series selector. The builder renders them once, where
the selector is first consumed: after its window, as in
`rate(m[5m] offset 1h @ end())`, or after the bare selector when nothing
windows it. Never between a selector and its window, which does not parse. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--selector_modifiers))
- `show_error_budget` (Boolean) Show each window's remaining error budget beside its compliance. Both
numbers are already on every SLO row, so this costs no extra request.
- `slo_table_view` (String)
- `sort_by` (String)
- `sort_order` (String)
- `sorting` (Block, Optional) sortingSchema :357, defaulting to DEFAULT_SORTING :137. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--panel--query--sorting))
- `source` (String)
- `summary_type` (String) Scopes "summary" like `filters`. Defaults to "monitor", which is what the
widget did before this field existed — an older saved panel keeps its
behaviour rather than silently changing what each row means.
- `time_windows_json` (String) Which rollup windows "single" draws.

These four and no others, because these are the four the API computes.
getSLOMetricsForSLOs builds one CTE per window with a literal INTERVAL, so
the set is fixed server-side rather than parameterised — a document naming
"90 days" would describe a column no response carries. Widen this only
together with the query and the columns.

"last_28_days" is four whole weeks, deliberately not 30 days. Set with jsonencode().
- `value` (String)
- `variables` (List of String)
- `view_mode` (String) What "single" draws: the objective's own rollups, a per-group breakdown,
or both. Only meaningful for a GROUPED objective — the webapp falls back
to the rollups when a panel names an SLO with no groups, so a saved
document does not blank itself if its SLO changes shape.
- `visible` (Boolean)
- `viz_type` (String)
- `widget_type` (String) "single", not "summary": an unconfigured panel waits for an objective
rather than fetching a fleet-wide rollup nobody asked for. The webapp
moved to that default in #2388 and this side was missed, so a panel saved
without the field meant one widget to the browser and another to
ApplyDefaults. The two must agree — this is the number the published
schema hands every other consumer.
- `window` (String) The window the uptime covers, ending now. Absent, the panel's time range
applies: its config.timeFrame, else the dashboard's.
- `xaxis` (String) SPL/SQL-only visualisation hints (:642-656). "auto" means the formatter
infers the column.
- `yaxis_json` (String) yaxis is a LIST, not a string. It was a string until commit 2c8d7ab1a
(2026-08-07, "update y-axis handling to support multiple select"), which
changed the persisted type and added coerceYaxisColumns + yaxisColumnsSchema
(:571, :586) plus a coercion step in migrateToNewSchema (:854) so stored
documents holding `yaxis: "cpu"` keep that selection.

Worth noting what that change cost: it is a breaking type change to a
persisted field, and it is detected by sniffing `!Array.isArray(next.yaxis)`
because panels carry no version marker. With one, the migration would key
off the version instead of guessing from shape. Set with jsonencode().

<a id="nestedblock--tab--panel--query--column_field"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tab.panel.query.column_field`

Optional:

- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `field` (String) The field name to query.
- `is_attribute` (Boolean) Whether this is an attribute field.
- `type` (String) The data type of the field. Defaults to "string" rather than being
required, because stored rules genuinely arrive without it — a live traces
rule with 119 firing series carries
`groupBy: [{field: "workload", is_attribute: false}]` and no type at all.
Requiring it rejected a document the product itself wrote and is running.

"string" is the safe fill: a group-by key is a string, and the two places a
NUMERIC type is load-bearing declare their own, so an aggregation cannot
silently acquire a string column.

### Nested Schema for `tab.sub_grid.panel.config.value_options`

Optional:

- `calculation` (String) Optional on purpose. Absent means the number is computed over the whole

events, synthetics), so a unique count or percentile is exact; metrics
panels use the last value. Any value set here instead reduces the

<a id="nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tab.sub_grid.panel.query`

Optional:

- `aggregation_json` (String) Set with jsonencode().
- `chart_type` (String)
- `color_preference` (String)
- `column_field` (Block List) No .catch() on this one in the zod — the only member of the base without a
fallback. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--column_field))
- `display` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--display))
- `display_format` (String)
- `expression` (String)
- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `field_config` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--field_config))
- `filter` (Block, Optional) Which monitors a panel draws when it does not name them, or how it narrows
the ones it names. Every key present must match; within types and within
states any one value matches.

Labels are a map here and a list of "key:value" on the wire: the renderer
sends them as `labels` to POST /api/synthetics/uptimes. Types go as `types`.
That endpoint does not filter by state, so a states filter is resolved
through GET /api/synthetics/monitors?state=…, which carries each monitor's
state, and the uptimes are then fetched for the ids it returns. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--filter))
- `filter_mode` (String)
- `filters_json` (String) Label matchers for builder mode, keyed by label. Each value's prefix picks
its PromQL operator: `v` is `label="v"`, `-v` is `label!="v"`, `~re` is
`label=~"re"` and `-~re` is `label!~"re"`. So `-` alone excludes the empty
value (`label!=""`). A whole `$var` or `-$var` value stands for the
variable's selected values. Set with jsonencode().
- `function` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--function))
- `group_by` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--group_by))
- `group_by_dimensions` (List of String) Sections around the outermost level's tiles. Only dimensions that level
carries are accepted by kubeapi; a host has no namespace. Not `groupBy`,
which the logs and traces arms use for a list of field objects.
- `label` (String)
- `label_options_json` (String) labelOptionsSchema :344 — discriminated on `type`, defaulting to auto
(DEFAULT_LABEL_OPTIONS :133).

Three arms for two cases. The first is the concrete default instance, and it
has to be written with plain fields rather than `!` — a required field is
never concrete, so `*#AutoLabelOptions` would leave nothing for the default to
materialise. But a closed concrete arm rejects any member added later, and
unlike `aggregation` or `sortBy` the auto case had no open sibling to fall
through to: `{type: "auto", somethingNew: 1}` matched neither arm. #AutoLabel
is that sibling. Set with jsonencode().
- `level` (Block List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--level))
- `list` (List of String)
- `monitor_ids` (List of String) The monitors to draw, in display order unless display.sort says
otherwise. An id that no longer exists is reported by the API and
skipped.
- `objective_id` (String) The objective "single" draws. "" means none picked yet, which the webapp
renders as an empty panel rather than fetching.
- `objective_name` (String) The objective's name AS IT WAS when the panel was saved. A cache, not an
identifier — objectiveId is what names the SLO.

Persisted so an editor can label its picker before the lookup returns, and
so a DELETED objective can still be named rather than shown as a bare
uuid. Readers must prefer the live name: a rename would otherwise leave
every dashboard asserting the old one forever.
- `pagination` (Block, Optional) explorerPaginationSchema :369, defaulting to DEFAULT_PAGINATION :146. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--pagination))
- `promql` (String)
- `query` (String)
- `query_mode` (String)
- `rule_id` (String) The rule "graph" and "value" draw. "" means none picked yet, which the
webapp renders as an empty panel rather than fetching.
- `rule_name` (String) The rule's name AS IT WAS when the panel was saved. A cache, not an
identifier — ruleId is what names the rule.

Persisted so an editor can label its picker before the lookup returns, and
so a DELETED rule can still be named rather than shown as a bare uuid.
Readers must prefer the live name: a rename would otherwise leave every
dashboard asserting the old one forever.
- `selected_metric` (String) DEFAULT_METRIC :35. The editor substitutes this placeholder when the field
is missing and then PERSISTS it on the next save, so an omitted
selectedMetric is not neutral — it silently becomes a real query against an
unrelated metric.
- `selected_mode` (String)
- `selector_modifiers` (Block, Optional) Offset and @ on the series selector. The builder renders them once, where
the selector is first consumed: after its window, as in
`rate(m[5m] offset 1h @ end())`, or after the bare selector when nothing
windows it. Never between a selector and its window, which does not parse. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--selector_modifiers))
- `show_error_budget` (Boolean) Show each window's remaining error budget beside its compliance. Both
numbers are already on every SLO row, so this costs no extra request.
- `slo_table_view` (String)
- `sort_by` (String)
- `sort_order` (String)
- `sorting` (Block, Optional) sortingSchema :357, defaulting to DEFAULT_SORTING :137. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--sorting))
- `source` (String)
- `summary_type` (String) Scopes "summary" like `filters`. Defaults to "monitor", which is what the
widget did before this field existed — an older saved panel keeps its
behaviour rather than silently changing what each row means.
- `time_windows_json` (String) Which rollup windows "single" draws.

These four and no others, because these are the four the API computes.
getSLOMetricsForSLOs builds one CTE per window with a literal INTERVAL, so
the set is fixed server-side rather than parameterised — a document naming
"90 days" would describe a column no response carries. Widen this only
together with the query and the columns.

"last_28_days" is four whole weeks, deliberately not 30 days. Set with jsonencode().
- `value` (String)
- `variables` (List of String)
- `view_mode` (String) What "single" draws: the objective's own rollups, a per-group breakdown,
or both. Only meaningful for a GROUPED objective — the webapp falls back
to the rollups when a panel names an SLO with no groups, so a saved
document does not blank itself if its SLO changes shape.
- `visible` (Boolean)
- `viz_type` (String)
- `widget_type` (String) "single", not "summary": an unconfigured panel waits for an objective
rather than fetching a fleet-wide rollup nobody asked for. The webapp
moved to that default in #2388 and this side was missed, so a panel saved
without the field meant one widget to the browser and another to
ApplyDefaults. The two must agree — this is the number the published
schema hands every other consumer.
- `window` (String) The window the uptime covers, ending now. Absent, the panel's time range
applies: its config.timeFrame, else the dashboard's.
- `xaxis` (String) SPL/SQL-only visualisation hints (:642-656). "auto" means the formatter
infers the column.
- `yaxis_json` (String) yaxis is a LIST, not a string. It was a string until commit 2c8d7ab1a
(2026-08-07, "update y-axis handling to support multiple select"), which
changed the persisted type and added coerceYaxisColumns + yaxisColumnsSchema
(:571, :586) plus a coercion step in migrateToNewSchema (:854) so stored
documents holding `yaxis: "cpu"` keep that selection.

Worth noting what that change cost: it is a breaking type change to a
persisted field, and it is detected by sniffing `!Array.isArray(next.yaxis)`
because panels carry no version marker. With one, the migration would key
off the version instead of guessing from shape. Set with jsonencode().

<a id="nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--column_field"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tab.sub_grid.panel.query.column_field`

Optional:

- `extra_json` (String) Members the schema does not describe, as JSON. Kept so nothing is lost. Set with jsonencode().
- `field` (String) The field name to query.
- `is_attribute` (Boolean) Whether this is an attribute field.
- `type` (String) The data type of the field. Defaults to "string" rather than being
required, because stored rules genuinely arrive without it — a live traces
rule with 119 firing series carries
`groupBy: [{field: "workload", is_attribute: false}]` and no type at all.
Requiring it rejected a document the product itself wrote and is running.

"string" is the safe fill: a group-by key is a string, and the two places a
NUMERIC type is load-bearing declare their own, so an aggregation cannot
silently acquire a string column.

- `show_apdex` (Boolean) Show each monitor's apdex (0 to 1) beside its uptime. Apdex is null for
a monitor whose runs in the range carry no apdex threshold.
- `sort` (String) How rows are ordered. Unset, they keep the order the API returned: the
order of monitorIds when the panel names monitors, by name otherwise.
- `thresholds` (Block, Optional) Uptime percentages a monitor is coloured by: at or above `good` is healthy,
at or above `warn` a warning, below it failing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tab--sub_grid--panel--query--display--thresholds))

<a id="nestedblock--variable"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variable`

Optional:

without escaping.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Bring an existing dashboard under Terraform by its id. Export to Terraform in
# the UI shows this command with the id filled in.
terraform import kubesense_dashboard.checkout 2b0e8f3a-6a51-4f3e-9b8e-0c7d1f2a9e41
```
